exclusion_reason: The recompiled-vs-interpreted speedup is measured on this host and clears the interpreter multiple by a wide margin, but the >=50%-of-native fraction cannot be measured because no native-execution baseline exists, and the multiple is not certified against the BPTK-002 reference desktop, so the bar is not cleared.
promotion_trigger: Promote to passing when the same frozen workload clears both the >=5x interpreter multiple and the >=50% native fraction on the pinned BPTK-002 reference desktop.
expected_failing_assertion: No native-execution baseline exists, so the native fraction of GS-093 is unmeasured and the bar stays red even though the interpreter multiple clears here.
active_gate_evidence: test/performance.test.mjs runs the frozen CPU-bound workload through both the interpreter oracle and the recompiled WebAssembly module (lib/performance.mjs benchmarkRecompiler), asserts the recompiled path computes the identical register state and instruction count (is_equivalent) with fallback_count zero, and asserts the recompiled throughput exceeds the interpreter with a real interpreter_multiple above one; it also pins that native_fraction is null, measured_on_reference_desktop is false, and is_bar_cleared stays false with the native-baseline and reference-desktop blockers declared.
procedure: Run the frozen workload recompiled, interpreted, and native.
Compute both ratios on the same machine and revision.
Compare against the declared multiple and fraction.
pass_criterion: The interpreter multiple clears the declared bar.
The native fraction clears the declared bar.
